title: Paco León, Miren Ibarguren and Alicia Falcó star in 'Rata', Netflix's new and exciting comedy
summary: Where does being a saver end and being a penny-pincher begin?
body_markdown:
Entertainment


13 October 2026


Global


Spain


Link copied to clipboard


[DOWNLOAD THE FIRST IMAGE](https://assetshare.netflixstudios.com/713920b8-4bc0-40a4-89e3-2770b947644d)


Netflix today announced the start of filming on


Rata


, a remake of the 2016 French film


Radin


, by Laurent Turner, Nicolas Cuche and Fred Cavayé. The comedy stars


Paco León


(


Aida: The Movie, Sin instrucciones


) alongside


Miren Ibarguren


(


La que se avecina, You Keep the Kids


) and


Alicia Falcó


(


The Map of Longing, Billionaires' Bunker


), and is directed by


Oriol Pérez Alcaraz


(


La casa nostra


). Filming of this Fasten International Films production for Netflix will take place at various locations in Madrid.


Federico (


Paco León


) counts the minutes of his showers, the watts and even his sighs. His perfectly controlled life as a penny-pincher is turned upside down when Laura (


Alicia Falcó


), the daughter he never knew he had, shows up. Determined to wreck his meticulous system of saving and to set him up with Valentina (


Miren Ibarguren


), Laura will show him that some things have no price.


Rata is written by


Eric Navarro


and


Natalia Durán


, directed by


Oriol Pérez Alcaraz


, executive produced by


Claudia Calviño


, and produced by


Gaël Nouaille


and


Adria Monés


, with


Andreu Ortoll


as director of photography.


About Fasten Films


At Fasten Films, we tell original stories that entertain, inspire, and move audiences. In 2026, Fasten had a prominent presence at the Cannes Film Festival, where it has premiered three feature films:


The End of It


(Maria Martínez Bayona, 2026, starring Rebecca Hall, Noomi Rapace, Gael García Bernal, and David Verdaguer); Morocco’s Oscar submission,


Strawberries


(Laïla Marrakchi, 2026); and the United Kingdom’s Oscar submission,


Rehearsals for a Revolution


(Pegah Ahangarani, 2026), winner of The Golden Eye. We are currently developing and producing new projects featuring talents such as Mar Coll, Marcel Barrena, Maria Martínez Bayona, Jorge Dorado, Ana Katz, Carlos Marques-Marcet, and Nely Reguera, among others.
